sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Traffic signs

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
The octagon demands a complete stop before giving way, whereas the upside-down triangle only requires yielding the right-of-way to cross or merging traffic [A01].
Why it matters: group shapes; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F02; confusables sec07-F02, sec07-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
The yellow-and-black circle is the advance warning of a railroad crossing, while the pentagon marks a school zone or school crossing [A01].
Why it matters: group shapes; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F06; confusables sec07-F06, sec07-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
The pennant marks where a no-passing zone begins, while the right-side-up triangle with a red border and orange center marks a slow-moving or emergency-stopped vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: group shapes; difficulty high; prereq sec07-F05; confusables sec07-F05, sec07-F09 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A02
Most regulatory signs are white with black letters, a red sign with white letters carries a very important message, and a red outline with a diagonal bar always means no [A02].
Why it matters: group regulatory-colors; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F10; confusables sec07-F10, sec07-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A02
A speed limit sign is a regulation showing the fastest legal speed in optimal conditions, whereas a black-on-yellow advisory speed sign on a ramp only recommends a maximum safe speed [A02].
Why it matters: group speed-signs; difficulty high; prereq sec07-F17; confusables sec07-F17, sec07-F19 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
Warning diamonds are yellow with black letters, but pedestrian and school warning signs may instead be yellow-green with black letters [A03].
Why it matters: group warning-colors; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F18; confusables sec07-F18, sec07-F24 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A04
Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right tell the driver to bear right, and stripes sloping downward to the left tell the driver to bear left [A04].
Why it matters: group work-zones; difficulty high; prereq sec07-F28; confusables sec07-F28 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A05
White on green guides direction, white on blue marks motorist services, and white on brown marks parks and public recreation areas [A05].
Why it matters: group guide-colors; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F32; confusables sec07-F32 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A05
State and United States route markers are generally black on white, while interstate markers are red, white and blue [A05].
Why it matters: group route-markers; difficulty low; prereq sec07-F35; confusables sec07-F35, sec07-F32 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
A dual turn lane sign marks a center lane reserved for left turns from either direction and never for passing, while lane direction signs at divider openings only remind you which side of the divider to use [A02].
Why it matters: group lane-signs; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F14; confusables sec07-F14, sec07-F15 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A01
A school zone reaches one hundred twenty-five feet along the street from the school grounds, and its fifteen miles per hour limit applies when children are present or when specified [A01].
Why it matters: group school-zone; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F07; confusables sec07-F07, sec07-F08 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0044]
